one_line_contribution: Memory-item utility is claimed to fall with the *directed* writer to reader capability gap (frontier-written items hurt an 8B reader while 8B-written items do not hurt a 14B reader), the cure is reader-side *selection* rather than reader *authorship*, and coupling a GEPA-style optimizer to the memory bank hides that harm at net accuracy while it survives in the break-count decomposition.
closest_prior_work: AMD / Agent Memory Distillation (arXiv:2608.07169, 2026) is the sharpest threat, and the proposal itself concedes why: AMD already reports that teacher-to-student memory 'yields inconsistent improvements and in several cases degrades performance' and that transfer quality 'depends on both teacher accuracy and teacher-student compatibility.' Harm plus a compatibility term is therefore prior. Rosetta Memory (2606.07711) independently formalizes write-model/read-model dependence. What is left to this proposal is a sign on an already-reported compatibility term, a fix/break decomposition, and the masking result -- a refinement, not a new phenomenon. Secondarily, the on-policy distillation line (self-generated data beating teacher-generated data because of distribution mismatch) makes the signed direction the expected outcome rather than a surprising one; the proposal's defense (the training-free regime does not entail it) is fair but makes the prediction low-information if it confirms.
strongest_objection: Prediction 5, the masking claim -- the most novel thing in the proposal -- is not testable at the stated design. It asks that the H-vs-I (self bank vs frontier bank under GEPA instructions) net-accuracy difference 'falls below the MDE,' i.e. it claims a null. Establishing that an effect has been masked requires showing the H-I difference is *smaller* than the B-C difference, an interaction whose variance is roughly sqrt(2) that of a single contrast, giving an MDE of ~6 points by the proposal's own arithmetic -- while the base effect it is supposed to shrink is predicted at only 4 points. The shrinkage the paper wants to report is therefore undetectable by construction. Worse, H, I, G and J each rest on a *single* GEPA optimization run, and the variance of GEPA's own search is never estimated anywhere: run M re-seeds decoding only, not optimization. The proposal's own Measurement section reports pilot drift of 5-14 points and a treatment-free replicate that mimicked the best real treatment; a single-seed prompt-search difference is exactly the kind of quantity that noise floor swallows. The identical arithmetic sinks the primary asymmetry claim: run D's mirror cell (14B reads 8B bank) carries only one bank replicate, so by the proposal's own rule it is 'directional only,' yet prediction 1's difference-in-differences -- the sole contrast that discriminates the signed account from Rosetta/MemCollab's symmetric one -- is computed from it. The cells that decide the paper are the ones run at the lowest power tier.
what_would_fix_it: Reallocate episodes from the cells that the proposal already admits are uninformative to the cells that decide the claims. Drop run L outright -- the proposal concedes n=300 gives MDE 6-7 points and that it 'will not read a sub-6-point null there as evidence of parity,' so it cannot exclude a stylistic-affinity effect of the same size as the primary effect and buys nothing -- and spend those four runs on (a) a second bank replicate for both run D direction cells, so the primary difference-in-differences carries estimable bank variance, and (b) a second independent GEPA optimization seed for G/H/I/J, so the masking difference can be separated from prompt-search variance. Restate prediction 5 as a prespecified interaction (or a TOST equivalence test with a stated margin, e.g. the H-I difference is bounded within +/-2 points while B-C exceeds 4), never as 'falls below the MDE.' Add the two missing controls on run K (below). Finally, add a paraphrase arm -- the 8B rewrites frontier items verbatim in content but in its own idiom -- to separate 'the advice names actions beyond the reader's competence' from 'the surface form is off-distribution'; without it, the executability readout in prediction 7 is consistent with both, and only the first supports the capability-gap framing.
missing_baseline: Run K has no controls of its own, and it carries the mechanism claim. Two are needed. (1) Reader-probe selection applied to the *self* bank. If probe filtering lifts the self bank by as much as it lifts the frontier bank, 'selection, not authorship' collapses into 'filtering helps any bank,' and prediction 4(a) becomes uninterpretable. (2) A random-subset frontier bank matched to K's *surviving item count*, not merely to its injected token budget. K keeps only items that survive three probe replays and then pads to the token budget -- padding equalizes tokens but not the number of distinct actionable recommendations, and the track's own starting position is that injection volume (seven items to three), not content, was the causal lever that eliminated harm. As written, K's predicted 50% recovery is fully explained by the already-known volume effect, and the proposal never rules it out. A third omission: no arm has the 8B *author* a bank from the 14B's traces, the mirror of run E; without it, 'who acted' and 'who wrote' are decomposed in only one direction.
preprint_collision: Well above the norm and it should be credited as such: it names specific arXiv identifiers, concedes that AMD already reports both the harm and a compatibility term, states plainly that 'the novelty of cross-model agent memory transfers badly is gone as of mid-2026,' names the residual risk (a self-written-bank ablation in some appendix), and reports an OpenReview check. I found no preprint that makes the masking claim. But the check searches for collisions on the phenomenon it has already surrendered, not on the claims it is defending. Nothing is searched for reader-verified or rollout-gated memory admission -- success-gated and validated-insight writing is already routine practice in the ExpeL/ReasoningBank line, so 'reader-in-the-loop selection helps' is close to a described technique and the genuinely new part is only the selection-vs-authorship *contrast*; nothing is searched for optimizer-memory interaction or attribution in coupled systems, which is where the paper's freshest claim lives. No search queries, dates, or venue scope are given. So: an honest, unusually specific check that is nonetheless aimed at the wrong target, and it leaves the two surviving contributions unverified.
